newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher in seasonal correction.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher in seasonal correction.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a possible seasonal harvest correction with commercial demand also mentioned, traders said.
"The chart looks like it wants to be a bottom but it also might be a bear flag. My thinking is it might be a bottom," said Tom Levis, Prudential Securities grains analyst.
New crop July recently set six-month lows and neared a three-year low for a nearby CBOT wheat futures contract.

Showers in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region where harvesting is occuring, also led to support, sources said. The weather was slowing wheat combining but reports were still coming in of excellent wheat yields, even in areas that were hit by a mid-April freeze, traders said.
"They're getting 35 to 40 bushels (per acre) on wheat that was expected to yield 15 after the freeze," a trader said.
CBOT SRW wheat closed two cents per bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with July down 3/4 at $3.31-3/4 a bushel. September was up one at $3.40.

FIMAT Futures bought two million bushels of December and bought one million September and sold one million July, traders said. Continental Grain bought one-half million September, Cargill Inc bought 300,000 bushels of September and SAK Futures bought one million September, traders said.

In spread trading, E.D. and F. Man International did two million July/December at 20-1/2 cents, premium September, traders said. Lind Waldock did 1.5 million bushels of December/July at 20 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, below the 26,859 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 250 September $3.60 puts at 22-1/2 cents, Refco Inc sold 250 September $3.50 calls at eight cents and First Options bought 125 September $3.20 puts at 3-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,800 contracts, below the 6,035 traded Tuesday.
